brief: Deutsche Bank's daily macro wrap: hopes for a diplomatic solution in the Middle East, spurred by Trump's comment he'd meet Iran's President at the UN, pushed Brent briefly below $100/bbl and drove European gas futures down 7.88%. That eased inflation fears and cut the priced probability of a second ECB hike this year from 52% to 40%, though Fed pricing held near 33bps of year-end hikes amid hawkish comments from Goolsbee (AI-driven demand overheating) and Musalem (current rate 'on the accommodative side'). Lower energy prices drove European sovereign yields to their biggest declines since May; the US 10yr fell less, to 4.95%, flattening the 2s10s curve to its flattest since February 2025. Equities rallied broadly: the S&P neared its record high, the Nasdaq and Magnificent 7 hit new records, led by Meta (Muse AI optimism) and AMD (new $1trn valuation). Overnight, Bessent's threat to cut off Iranian airlines pushed oil back up. Separately, US-China truce-extension talks continued ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting, and Germany's CDU missed the 5% threshold in a state election, though Merz said his coalition holds.
